title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 650 bis–787 of the sequel to La Longue Marche): Grothendieck is working out by hand the low-dimensional Teichmüller groups and their Galois-type automorphism groups, in two parallel settings. One is group schemes over a base S (underlined letters); the other is profinite groups (hatted or unadorned letters). The objects as I read them:
- H^+ is a discrete or profinite group of modular type (presumably SL2-like, generated by ρ and σ).
- M is an abelian 'lattice' group (rank-2, with M^ its profinite completion), acted on by H^+ and twisted by a cyclotomic character χ.
- B^+ (also written 𝔊^+) is an extension of H^+ by M.
- Φ_12^* (transcribed O_12^*) is a unit-type group with a cyclotomic character χ and homomorphisms ν, ν_2, where ν_2 takes values in Z/2. Its profinite incarnation is Ẑ^*.
- G_{ρ,σ} is the group of automorphisms (or symmetries) of B^+ normalising the data ρ, σ. It is an extension of Φ_12^* × H^+ by M.
- Φ_12^*'' = ker ν_2 is an index-≤2 subgroup, and G''_{ρ,σ} is the preimage of Φ_12^*'' × H^+.

The previous page computes the centraliser in G_{ρ,σ} of a lifted subgroup H(ρ',σ') over H^+. This lifted subgroup is the image of a splitting of B^+ → H^+ given by new generators ρ', σ'.
- That centraliser lies in Φ_12^*·(M × μ). Its elements have the form λ ω^i u_μ, with ω an element of order 2.
- Commuting with σ' forces ν_2(μ)=0, i.e. μ ∈ Φ_12^*''.

This page draws the conclusions.
- (271): the centraliser T of such a lifted copy of H^+ sits in an exact sequence 1 → M^ (or the relevant finite piece) → T → Φ_12^*'' → 1.
- (272): T^♮ = T ∩ G^♮_{ρ,σ} maps isomorphically onto Φ_12^*''. So T^♮ is a partial section of G^♮ over Φ_12^*''.

First corollary (scheme version):
- The extension G_{ρ,σ} of Φ_12^* × H^+ by M is split over no non-empty base S.
- The restricted extension G''_{ρ,σ} of Φ_12^*'' × H^+ by M splits over every base S.
- Any two splittings are conjugate by a unique section of M.
- Restriction to H^+ gives a bijection between splittings of G'' over Φ_12^*'' × H^+ and splittings of B^+ over H^+. In other words, every splitting of B^+ → H^+ extends uniquely to the Φ_12^*'' factor.

Second corollary (profinite version): the same statements hold with Ẑ^* in place of Φ_12^*, Ẑ^*'' in place of Φ_12^*'', and M^, B^ in place of M, B^+. The extension of Ẑ^* × H^+ by M^ is non-split. Over Ẑ^*'' × H^+ it splits, with splittings conjugate under a unique element of M^ and in bijection with splittings of B^ over H^+.

In cohomological terms:
- The class of the full extension is non-zero.
- Its restriction to the index-2 subgroup dies.
- H^1 is a torsor under M, since conjugation by M acts simply transitively.

The next page makes a splitting explicit by choosing a particular solution (a0, a1, b) = (1, 0, 0) of a0 − 2a1 + 3b − 1 = 0, i.e. ρ' = λ0 ρ, σ' = σ. It also writes the induced lift μ ↦ λ_∞^ν u_μ of Φ_12^*'' into G_{ρ,σ}.
errors: No mathematical error is detectable on this page; the claims are stated without proof here and rest on the computations of pp. 703–706.

Minor inconsistency in notation, probably a slip: the last line of the profinite corollary says 'scindages de G''_{ρ,σ} sur Ẑ^* × H^+'. It should read Ẑ^*'' × H^+, since over the full Ẑ^* there are no splittings.
In (271) the kernel is written M^ while the group T is written in scheme notation (underlined). This mixes the scheme and profinite notations, or else the 'M^' is a misreading.

ideas.what: Non-splitting of the extension of (cyclotomic units) × H^+ by the lattice M, with splitting after restriction to the index-2 kernel of ν_2
ideas.modern_name: Obstruction class in H^2 of an extension, killed on an index-2 subgroup; Galois-equivariant sections of the arithmetic fundamental group of modular/elliptic type
ideas.usually_credited_to: General extension theory (Eilenberg–MacLane); specific arithmetic-fundamental-group splitting questions are associated with Nakamura, Ihara and others for M_{1,1} / elliptic curves (unsure of the exact match)
ideas.where_published: Not in published texts; La Longue Marche (1981) only sketches the Teichmüller program without such explicit computations

ideas.what: Splittings of G'' are a torsor under M (unique conjugating section), and restriction gives a bijection with splittings of B^+ over H^+
ideas.modern_name: H^1-torsor description of splittings; uniqueness of the extension of sections to the Galois / cyclotomic factor
ideas.where_published: General formalism in SGA 1 / Giraud; specific statement unpublished

ideas.what: Parallel treatment of the same extension over arbitrary base schemes S (group schemes) and profinitely
ideas.modern_name: Group-scheme models of profinite Teichmüller-type groups (twisted constant groups)

missed.claim: An explicit computation of a non-split extension of Ẑ^* × H^+ by M^ that becomes split on the index-2 kernel of ν_2. Splittings are classified up to unique M^-conjugacy and identified with splittings of B^ over H^+. This is a concrete detail of Grothendieck's unpublished 1981-era Teichmüller computations; it is likely equivalent to known facts about Galois sections in the genus-1 (or modular) case, but this presentation is unrecorded.
missed.quote: L'ext. G_{ρ,σ} de Ẑ^* × H^+ par M^ n'est pas scindée. Celle de G''_{ρ,σ} de Ẑ^*'' × H^+ par M^ est scindée, et deux scindages sont conjugués par un unique élément de M^
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents how Grothendieck handled the 'sign' (ν_2) obstruction in the arithmetic Teichmüller tower in low dimension. This is relevant to historians of the Grothendieck–Teichmüller program, but probably not new mathematics.

deep.surprise_reason: These are careful but routine extension and splitting computations inside Grothendieck's unpublished Teichmüller notes. The index-2 obstruction is a nice explicit detail, but nothing here seems beyond what specialists in GT and anabelian geometry know.
transcription_corrections: 'n'est scindée sur aucun bon S non vide' should read 'sur aucune base S non vide'; likewise 'sur tout bon S' should read 'sur toute base S'.
'une bijection des Vues des scindages' should read 'une bijection de l'ens. des scindages'.
'O_12^*' is probably the same symbol as Φ_12^* on the previous page.
Equation numbers are (271) and (272), not (27.1) and (27.2); the digits are overwritten in the manuscript.
In the first corollary, 'scindages de B^+ sur H^+' has B^+ written as a stylised 𝔅 or 𝔊^+, consistent with the 𝔊^+ on the next page.
The struck-through word under the first line is 'une suite', a false start.
